systematic_mappings.why: The convention every module of this lane uses.
systematic_mappings.affects: every entry that reads a report field

systematic_mappings.from: f-string ':.2f' formatting of a percentage and a rate
systematic_mappings.why: D-0104. Python's formatter rounds half to even and toFixed rounds half away from zero, and `total * 100 / cohort_size` produces exact ties -- one model response over 800 cohort runs is 0.125 per 100 runs. A rendered figure is a parity surface (interlock#74 AC3).

The source reads the column names off the cursor so a second hand-written list cannot drift from the statement. better-sqlite3 returns objects keyed by the statement's own output names, which is the same property with nothing to keep in step.

Python sorts by code point and JavaScript's default sort by UTF-16 code unit; an invocation id is caller-supplied, so the divergence is reachable, and the itemisation order is part of what D-0040 asks to be byte-reproducible.
The library's own pragma surface. The forged state -- a usage_status outside the CHECK, as written by a build with a wider vocabulary -- is unchanged.

systematic_mappings.from: pytest's `db` fixture and try/finally connection pairs
systematic_mappings.why: The convention every measurement test file in this port uses.
systematic_mappings.affects: every entry that touches a database

systematic_mappings.from: Python int arithmetic over the projected columns
systematic_mappings.to: safeIntegers(true) on the cohort statement and BigInt accumulation
systematic_mappings.why: Raised by the codex review gate. Python's int is unbounded and sums these exactly; better-sqlite3's default returns a JavaScript number and rounds 9007199254740993 to ...992 on the way in, so every AC-9 figure would be computed over values the database does not hold (D-0007, docs/sqlite-value-contract.md). The sums are BigInt and each total is converted at the boundary where it becomes a report field.
systematic_mappings.affects: every entry that reads a token or response figure

target_only_tests.note: Target-only tests translate no source case and are NOT counted as ported coverage. All eleven close gaps a 32-mutation sweep found, and all eleven are INHERITED: each mutation was applied to interlock's own ac9.py at 65f36c5 and its 23 cases stayed green (measured, not inferred). Each is recorded with its verdict under mutation_sweep and each was confirmed to kill its mutation and only its mutation. A twelfth is different in kind: a PORT DIVERGENCE the codex review gate found, with no inherited counterpart because the difference does not exist in Python. A thirteenth is the evidence for D-0107, the one place this port deliberately and permanently diverges from interlock: the header's acceptance predicate now agrees with the report's. See divergences. Further cases were added by the D-0109 / D-0110 remediation belt, which repaired defects this ledger had disclosed (and, in four modules, defects it had not): each is the evidence for a divergence recorded above. The D-0109 belt's follow-up added an 'every externally-supplied field at once' case for this renderer. It is structural rather than per-field: a case that drives ONE field hostile passes as soon as any other field is escaped, which is how four review rounds each found one more raw field. scripts/escaping-coverage.mjs measures whether it actually covers this module's reportValue sites by removing each in turn.

notes_on_exports.why: The fourth module of this lane to carry one (false-termination, cohort, shadow, canary are the others). Python namespaces them per module and a flat barrel cannot; each module still exports the bare name under its own path.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: The bounded and sensitivity figures are computed over different populations: the bound can only reach missing rows that carry a ceiling AND finished, while the p95 imputation covers every missing row.
inherited_limitations.note: Deliberate and reproduced. The source states it in a comment at the point of computation: it is the difference between 'what can be bounded' and 'what can be guessed at', and the report prints both itemisations beside both figures. A reader who wants one population for both has to decide what to do about a row with no ceiling, which is the decision section 2.4 refuses to make silently.
inherited_limitations.where_a_fix_belongs: nowhere; the asymmetry is the finding.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: A percentage rendered through the report's percent() helper cannot be driven onto an exact two-decimal tie by any input this schema admits, so the half-to-even rule is unexercised on that path.
inherited_limitations.note: Measured rather than assumed. A tie needs the value to be a dyadic rational of the form k/8, and percent()'s inputs are coverage ratios (k/n) and reductions (1 - a/b), neither of which lands exactly there -- a scan of every k/n with n up to 4000 found no input on which formatFixed and toFixed disagree. rate()'s input is total * 100 / cohortSize, which IS dyadic at 100/800 = 0.125, so the rule is pinned there by a target-only case. Substituting toFixed in percent() alone is therefore an EQUIVALENT MUTANT for constructible data; substituting it in rate() is not, and is caught.
inherited_limitations.where_a_fix_belongs: nowhere; the helper is correct and the class is simply unreachable through it.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: A total that does not fit a JavaScript number exactly is REFUSED (FigureExceedsExactRangeRefused) where interlock would carry and print it.
inherited_limitations.note: A disclosed divergence in the refusing direction, introduced by the fix above. Python's unbounded int has no such boundary; JavaScript's number does, and this module's subject is a figure that quietly differs from the measurement -- printing a rounded token total would be that failure exactly. Nothing an actual ledger can hold reaches it: 2^53 output tokens is nine quadrillion. The new target-only case builds the state deliberately, one row at MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (carried) and two (refused).
inherited_limitations.where_a_fix_belongs: nowhere while the report field is a JavaScript number; carrying BigInt out to consumers would change the package's public shape for a value no ledger produces.

mutation_sweep.ran: 32 mutations, one per property the ported cases claim to pin, 2026-08-22

survivors.mutation: the p95 rank rounds instead of taking the ceiling
survivors.verdict: inherited blind spot, closed with a target-only test
survivors.note: The ported case uses 20 covered values, where ceil(0.95*20) and round(0.95*20) are both 19. At 11 values they part company (11 against 10). The new case uses 11.

survivors.mutation: an empty covered sample yields a p95 of 0 instead of None
survivors.verdict: inherited blind spot, closed with a target-only test
survivors.note: The ported empty-cohort case reaches the same null through a different door -- with no runs every per-100 figure is null anyway. The new case has a real cohort and an entirely uncovered ledger, where 0 would turn 'no covered sample, so no p95' into a measurement.

survivors.mutation: the sensitivity total drops the p95 term
survivors.verdict: inherited blind spot, closed with a target-only test
survivors.note: No case on either side pins the sensitivity TOTAL; the bound case asserts only inequalities, which survive the term's removal. Without it the figure is observed alone, which is the treat-missing-as-zero number section 2.4 forbids.

survivors.mutation: the reduction is clamped at zero
survivors.verdict: inherited blind spot, closed with a target-only test
survivors.note: The source says in terms that it is not clamped: a negative reduction means Interlock used MORE than the baseline and the report is obliged to print it. No case on either side produces one, and a clamp is the flattering direction -- it would report parity where the measurement says regression.

survivors.mutation: the baseline normalises per run instead of per 100 runs
survivors.verdict: inherited blind spot, closed with a target-only test
survivors.note: Every ported assertion about a reduction is relative -- an ordering or an equality between two figures -- so dropping the factor of 100 changes every number and fails nothing. The new case pins one figure against arithmetic done in the test.

survivors.mutation: a baseline with zero responses or zero tokens is accepted
survivors.verdict: inherited blind spot, closed with a target-only test
survivors.note: The ported case covers only the zero-RUN branch, on both sides. The other branch is the one that would print as a 100 percent reduction no matter what Interlock did.

survivors.mutation: the unattributed window becomes inclusive at the period end
survivors.verdict: inherited blind spot, closed with a target-only test
survivors.note: No case on either side puts a run-less invocation on the boundary, so a <= would move one invocation per report and show up nowhere else.

survivors.mutation: the invocation rows are not ordered by id
survivors.verdict: inherited blind spot, closed with a target-only test
survivors.note: Every ported case itemises at most one id. D-0040 asks a report to be byte-reproducible and the itemisation order is part of the bytes.

survivors.mutation: the cohort query drops its 500-id chunking
survivors.verdict: inherited blind spot, closed with a target-only test
survivors.note: No case on either side has a cohort of more than a handful of runs. The ceiling was measured on this build during the cohort belt (32,766 parameters succeed, 32,767 fails); the new case builds a 33,000-run cohort and attaches the invocation to the LAST run, so a loop that stopped after one chunk reports an empty ledger rather than crashing.

survivors.mutation: the report's rate() helper uses toFixed instead of formatFixed
survivors.verdict: inherited blind spot, closed with a target-only test
survivors.note: Every percentage in the ported cases is a round number, so toFixed passes all of them. One model response over 800 cohort runs is exactly 0.125 per 100 runs, where Python rounds to 0.12 and toFixed to 0.13 (D-0104). The same substitution in percent() survives and is recorded above as an equivalent mutant: its inputs cannot reach a tie.

survivors.verdict: inherited blind spot, closed with a target-only test
survivors.note: The ported case asserts the sentence is PRESENT at full coverage; nothing asserted it is absent otherwise. Printed unconditionally it tells a reader the three figures agree at exactly the moment they do not.

mutation_sweep.note: All eleven survivors were re-run against the new target-only cases and each is now killed by its own case and no other, with one recorded refinement: the toFixed substitution kills only on the rate() path, and the percent() path is an equivalent mutant for the reasons under inherited_limitations.

divergences.behaviour: ImputationRule carries unconfirmedResponseCount as well as unboundedMissing, its supportsAcceptanceClaim requires both to be zero, and the header prints the new count. interlock's header carries only unboundedMissing.
divergences.note: An INHERITED DEFECT in interlock, fixed here on the operator's ruling of 2026-08-22 rather than reproduced. interlock's Ac9Report disqualifies on two populations and its header on one, so over a report containing an unfinished invocation the AC-9 section says the claim is unsupported and the header says it is supported -- and render.py puts both answers in ONE document (.header.imputation_rule.supports_acceptance_claim true, .sections.ac9.facts.imputation.supports_acceptance_claim false), measured against interlock at 65f36c5, not inferred. The lane's own recommendation was reproduce-and-disclose, consistent with the shadow caveat and the provenance ORDER BY tie; the operator overrode it because those are omissions a reader can work around and this is a document asserting both true and false about one claim. interlock is frozen, so no upstream fix is coming: this is PERMANENT and continuo is authoritative.
divergences.parity_cost: continuo's rendered report differs from interlock's for any period containing an unfinished invocation: the header gains an imputation_rule.unconfirmed_response_count key and imputation_rule.supports_acceptance_claim flips to false. interlock#74 AC3 compares these documents, so this is the one place the two are intended to disagree, and it is reachable from this ledger.
divergences.evidence: test/measurement/ac9.test.ts::a deliberate divergence from interlock (target-only) > the header's acceptance predicate agrees with the report's
divergences.where_a_fix_belongs: nowhere; interlock is frozen and continuo is the authority for this field.

divergences.behaviour: renderAc9Report escapes the itemised invocation ids before printing them. interlock interpolates them raw.
divergences.note: This entry is NEW: nothing was disclosed here before. The inventory the operator asked for on 2026-08-22 was compiled from the LEDGERS, which recorded three instances of this class, and the sweep that followed found the same class in four more renderers by reading them. That the ledger showed fewer instances than the code held is itself worth recording: a disclosure list is only as complete as the pass that produced it. ai_invocation.invocation_id is unconstrained TEXT and the three itemisations -- AC-1 violations, unbounded_missing, unconfirmed response count -- each print `      <id>`. A forged line in the unbounded_missing list changes what a reader believes about whether the report can support an acceptance claim. Verified the way lane C's 'green guarantees nothing' note asks: the reportValue call was reverted at this site and the case was confirmed to fail FOR THAT REASON.
divergences.parity_cost: continuo's rendered report differs from interlock's wherever an invocation id is not printable ASCII.
